title: Bedlam Series Record: OU vs Oklahoma State From 1904 to 2023
question: What is Oklahoma's all-time record against Oklahoma State, and why did Bedlam stop?
answer: Oklahoma leads the Bedlam football series 91-20-7. The rivalry began with a 75-0 OU win in Guthrie in 1904, and the annual series went on hold after Oklahoma State's 27-24 win in 2023, when OU left the Big 12 for the SEC.
summary: OU leads Bedlam 91-20-7 after the 2023 game. From a 75-0 win in 1904 Guthrie to OSU's 27-24 finale, here's how the annual rivalry went on hold.
body: Bedlam started before Oklahoma was even a state. In November 1904, Oklahoma and Oklahoma A&M (today's Oklahoma State) met in Guthrie, then the territorial capital, and OU won 75-0. That remains the widest margin in series history.

The first game also produced Bedlam's best legend. A punt by A&M was blown backward by the wind, past the kicker and down a hill into a half-frozen creek. Players from both sides went in after it, and an Oklahoma player came up with the ball for a touchdown. As for the name, nobody knows exactly where it came from. One early use was a 1917 Daily Oklahoman story describing the scene after A&M's 9-0 win over OU, while another tale credits a wild wrestling meet between the schools.
On the field, the series has been heavily crimson. Oklahoma entered the 2023 game leading 91-19-7, and OU once won 19 straight meetings from 1946 to 1964.

The most recent chapter belonged to the Cowboys. On November 4, 2023, in Stillwater, Oklahoma State beat No. 10 Oklahoma 27-24 behind Ollie Gordon II's 137 rushing yards and two touchdowns, making the all-time record 91-20-7. It was the last Bedlam game before Oklahoma left the Big 12 for the SEC in 2024, which ended the annual conference matchup, and the next football meeting has not been set.

For now, Bedlam football lives in memory, from the 1904 creek touchdown to Oklahoma State's 38-35 overtime win in 2014 and OU's 62-52 shootout win in 2017. Fans on both sides are hoping it does not stay on hold forever.
